title: sIOPMP: Scalable and Efficient I/O Protection for TEEs
problem: I/O isolation in TEEs like Intel SGX/TDX and ARM TrustZone introduces significant performance overhead (20%+ throughput degradation) because traditional approaches like IOMMU and software I/O don't account for the different isolation requirements of I/O devices versus CPUs.
motivation: As TEEs become widely deployed, efficient I/O isolation is critical to enable practical performance for I/O-intensive workloads without sacrificing security.
method: sIOPMP uses a hardware-based system to control which devices can access protected memory in TEEs. It has three parts working together: first, a Multi-stage-Tree-based checker (a hierarchical structure that efficiently tracks memory regions) supporting over 1000 regions to grant or block access quickly; second, a classification system that divides devices into 'hot' (frequently accessed) or 'cold' (rarely accessed) categories with mountable entries to handle unlimited devices; third, a dynamic remapping mechanism that automatically moves devices between hot and cold groups based on how the workload actually uses them.
key_novelty: The system combines a Multi-stage-Tree-based checker (a hierarchical structure for fast memory protection lookups) with dynamic hot/cold device classification to support over 1000 memory regions and unlimited devices while adding almost no performance overhead.
contributions: Multi-stage-Tree-based checker supporting 1000+ hardware memory regions
Hot/cold device classification with mountable entry design for unlimited device support
Dynamic remapping mechanism for workload-aware device status switching
20-38% network throughput improvement over IOMMU and software I/O approaches
primary_theme: I/O isolation for trusted execution environments
